test_title: PYST 78: SSC CGL 2024 - Quantitative Aptitude (Held On 25 Sept, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: maths
question: From a point T, a tangent TP at point P, is drawn to a circle with centre O. A secant TQR (point Q is near to point T) is drawn from the point T. ∆PQR is inscribed into the circle by joining the points P, Q and R. Draw lines OQ and OR. If ∠PTQ is 27° and ∠TPQ = 55°, what is the degree measure of ∠ROQ?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The exterior angle of a triangle is equal to the sum of the two opposite interior angles. For ΔTQP, the exterior angle at Q is ∠PQR.

∠PQR = ∠PTQ + ∠TPQ = 27° + 55° = 82°.

By the Alternate Segment Theorem, the angle between the tangent TP and chord PQ equals the angle in the alternate segment: ∠PRQ = ∠TPQ = 55°.

In ΔPQR, ∠QPR = 180° − (∠PQR + ∠PRQ) = 180° − (82° + 55°) = 43°.

The central angle ∠ROQ is twice the angle subtended at the circumference by the same arc: ∠ROQ = 2 × ∠QPR = 2 × 43° = 86°.

**∴ The correct answer is 86°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

T is a point outside a circle with center O.

TP is a tangent to the circle at point P.

TQR is a secant intersecting the circle at points Q and R (with Q nearer to T).

∠PTQ = 27° and ∠TPQ = 55°.
